---
title: Packages and composition
---

cloudposterior composes two independently usable Python packages. Its `cp.cloud(model)` context manager remains the only global PyMC interceptor.

| Package | Owns | Public documentation |
|---|---|---|
| [pymc-monitor](https://github.com/justmytwospence/pymc-monitor) | Sampling engine, adaptive diagnostics, notebook/terminal displays and authenticated localhost dashboard | [Monitor API](https://justmytwospence.github.io/pymc-monitor/) |
| [pymc-cache](https://github.com/justmytwospence/pymc-cache) | Versioned model/data/kwargs fingerprints, policy-aware preflight, memory and disk storage | [Cache API](https://justmytwospence.github.io/pymc-cache/) |
| cloudposterior | Modal image/source delivery, volumes, progress transport, hosted dashboard, ntfy, model-map fanout and PyMC interception | [This API](reference/index.qmd) |

The monitor never imports the cache, and neither package imports Modal or cloudposterior. Each is on PyPI and usable on its own (`pip install pymc-monitor`, `pip install pymc-cache`); `pip install cloudposterior` pulls in both, as `pymc-monitor[notebook,dashboard]>=0.1,<0.2` and `pymc-cache>=0.1,<0.2`. Modal images install only pinned third-party dependencies and mount all three package sources and the monitor assets, so the remote worker runs exactly the code installed locally.

Local sampling uses the monitor engine with the captured original `pm.sample`, including `until=` and `init="prior"`. A local `dashboard=True` binds an authenticated loopback-only server; remote dashboard URLs are Modal-hosted and support phone access. PyMC/nutpie provide live draws and early stop; JAX samplers provide phase-level progress only. PyMC 5 and 6 are supported on their respective Python versions. Diagnostic thresholds are heuristics rather than guarantees.
